alalal-c46104-d1e101.summary: Rubric marking the second textual division of Distinction 37.

alalal-c46104-d1e110.summary: Quotes the incipit of the next part of Lombard's text: where did God dwell before there were saints?

alalal-c46104-d1e120.summary: Divides the second part of the first part of the distinction, in which Lombard raises three questions in three chapters: where God dwelt before the world; the exclusion of the error that the soul so fills the body that God cannot enter, held by the Tertullianist heretics who gave God and the soul human shape, head in head and feet in feet ('Sciendum est etiam'); and how God dwells in some who do not know him and not in some who do ('Illud quoque mirabile est').

alalal-c46104.summary: Division of the second section of the first part of Distinction 37. Lombard raises three questions: where God dwelt before the saints and the world existed; whether the soul fills the body so as to exclude God, an error of the Tertullianists, who imagined God and the soul in human shape; and how God dwells in some who do not know him but not in some who do.
